value.rationale: The decagonal prism and Desargues graph are two canonical nonisomorphic cubic 20-vertex networks. The numerical equality of *both* recurrent-state populations creates a natural test of whether recurrence counts can proxy for attraction outcomes. Their fixed-basin sizes differ by 70440 states and their equilibrium weight distributions are structurally different. The result is a complete natural finite dynamical invariant on a matched pair, with a counterexample to inferring basin size from attractor census, not an arbitrary new graph or an incremental rounding improvement.
